verdict: Below threshold (6.5 < 7.5): do not pass. The paper is rigorous, transparently pre-registered and internally consistent (spot-checked: every D value matches its RE/AE inputs, the hold-force savings, the tercile means against the CRC-point slip, the break-even arithmetic and the friction-window edges). But its central practical question, when the probe pays off, gets an answer that rests on untested conditions. The hold-force saving is modest (0.66 N / 9.3 % for the plug-in). The probe protocol's fixed force-time is repaid only after 17.74-27.07 s holds, and slip over holds that long was never simulated. The probe-vs-learner attribution flips between the registered relative metric and the post hoc absolute metric. Probe noise is assumed rather than grounded, and the marginal bound fails for the low-friction tercile under every arm. Everything is simulation-only, and no published controller was reproduced. The writing is honest but so heavily caveated and number-dense that the take-home message is hard to get out of the paper.
strengths: Strong statistical hygiene: five pre-registered confirmatory tests with Holm correction, TOST equivalence with a stated SESOI (0.10), an object-cluster bootstrap with lambda-hat refitted in each draw, a numbered deviation list (10 items) and explicit status codes (CONF/PRE/SEC/DESC/PH) on every row.

Fair and well-chosen comparators: the strongest friction-blind conformal baseline (CSF-1) was selected on a disjoint split before calibration or test access; a deployable family prior (CSF-fam) is included, and the paper honestly reports that it beats both tactile arms (C4, C5).

Clean experimental isolation: a friction-uninformative preload (32.7 N for every object, pad reading within 0.16 N) leaves the ramp-down onset as the only friction channel, and every rule receives the same true mass, acceleration and stratum.

Calibrates the physical binary slip loss (monotonised) rather than bisection labels. This is well motivated by the failed monotonicity gate (8/800), and the CRC formula and its marginal, in-expectation guarantee are stated correctly and with appropriate scope.

Honest boundary map: the saving is shown to reverse at high probe noise (sigma 0.4, plug-in), under narrow friction ranges (crossing between w 0.75 and 0.5) and against a sharp family prior; the force-time break-even against a no-probe grasp is reported even though it is unflattering.

The certificate's limits are exposed rather than hidden: 200 re-splits show 31.5-70 % with some stratum above alpha, and the post hoc friction-tercile breakdown shows that every arm exceeds alpha on low-friction objects.
Internal numerical consistency is high. Derived quantities (D from RE, D_abs from AE, percentage savings, break-even times, window edges, tercile averages) reproduce from the reported inputs.
weaknesses: [evidence-level] The headline practical question is unresolved. The probe's extra phases (about 18 N*s) are repaid only for holds of 17.74-27.07 s, but slip was simulated only over a 0.6 s disturbance window, so it is not shown that the certified hold force stays safe in the only regime where probing pays.

[evidence-level] Simulation only, with an assumed probe noise: rigid MuJoCo contact, a modelled taxel detector, and an added onset noise sigma = 0.2 that is not grounded in hardware or published detector error. The main effect changes sign across the sigma band (0.6486 -> -0.2065), so the primary result depends on an unvalidated parameter.

[evidence-level] Practical effect size is modest: 0.66 N (9.3 %) for the plug-in and 1.01 N (14.2 %) for the learned model in mean hold force, against a fixed protocol that preloads at 32.7 N and squeezes to about 49 N on every grasp. The relative-excess D values (about 0.43) overstate practical significance.

[evidence-level] The attribution is metric-dependent and rests on one model. The registered C2 equivalence (probe, not learner, carries the saving) holds only for relative excess, only on the matched route, only at sigma 0.2 and for a single training seed. On post hoc absolute excess the learner beats the plug-in by about as much as the probe beats the baseline (0.2667 vs 0.2372). Seed spread on C3 (0.3932-0.4494) exceeds half the SESOI.

[evidence-level] Three of the five confirmatory decisions (C1, C2, C4) rest on the test-slip-matched route, which uses test outcomes and is not a deployable certified rule. On the certified CRC route, C2 equivalence is not shown.

[evidence-level] The marginal guarantee leaves slippery objects under-protected: every arm exceeds alpha in the lowest-friction tercile (CSF-1 0.264, learned 0.173, plug-in 0.131), and on the correlated pool F1 exceeds alpha for three of four arms. No friction-conditional (Mondrian by mu-hat) calibration was run to show the force cost of fixing this.

[evidence-level] Missing comparators: no published tactile grip controller was reproduced (Khamis et al., Dong et al., Boonstra et al., Niu et al.), the reactive baseline is an acknowledged design artefact, and the natural family-prior + probe hybrid, which would answer whether touch still adds value when a prior exists, was not run.

[evidence-level] Offline CRC needs a replay of every calibration grasp at every grid force, so the primary method is not deployable. The deployable online route has ordering-only intervals, overshoot to 0.1389, no physical-replay oracle and an inconclusive efficiency test (H3).

[paper-level] Readability and message clarity: the abstract and the results are saturated with four-significant-figure numbers, route tags and caveats; the reader cannot easily extract a single take-home claim. Many qualifications are repeated almost verbatim across the abstract, introduction, Section 5, limitations and conclusion.

[paper-level] The title asks 'When does a friction-onset probe pay off?', but the honest answer in the text (only for untested long holds, only at low noise, only without a family prior) is not stated crisply up front; the framing still leans on relative-excess savings that the absolute and force-time analyses largely qualify.

[paper-level] The confirmatory narrative mixes several rounds (first-round pool, later rounds, fresh pool, post hoc rows), and Section 5.4 together with the mid-friction sub-pool row (sign depends on the grid) adds complexity with little interpretive payoff.
[paper-level] Figures exist only as generation prompts in HTML comments. Figure 1(b) and Figure 2 must be rendered from the analysis file before this version can be judged as a complete submission.
required_actions: [evidence-level] Simulate long holds (at least up to 30 s) at each arm's certified hold force, with repeated or sustained disturbances, and report the realised slip; without this, the break-even claim cannot support any recommendation to probe.

[evidence-level] Ground sigma: measure onset-detection error on hardware, or derive it from published incipient-slip detector error, and state where the real sensor falls on the sigma band; ideally add a small hardware validation of the probe and the hold-force rule.

[evidence-level] Run the family-prior + probe hybrid on the correlated pool, and a friction-conditional (Mondrian by mu-hat) CRC on the fresh pool, reporting the force cost of bringing the low-friction tercile to alpha or below.

[evidence-level] Run the learned model over multiple training seeds (e.g. seeds 0-4) for C2 and C5 and on the absolute-excess rows, and report the seed spread next to the single-seed confirmatory values.

[evidence-level] Reproduce at least one published friction-estimation-plus-margin controller (e.g. Khamis et al.) as a non-conformal comparator at matched slip, and test a lighter protocol (no squeeze, or an adaptive preload) to see whether the probe's fixed force-time, and hence the break-even, can be reduced.

[paper-level] Restructure the abstract and introduction around one crisp answer to the title question: probing helps under specific conditions; state the conditions and the modest absolute size up front, and move secondary numbers out of the abstract.

[paper-level] Present relative and absolute excess (and force-time) together as the main cost picture, rather than leading with the registered relative metric and qualifying it later; say plainly that the probe-vs-learner attribution is unresolved across metrics.

[paper-level] Cut the repeated caveats (state each once, in limitations, and refer back to it), reduce reported precision to 2-3 significant figures in the prose, and trim or move the earlier-round material (Section 5.4, the mid-friction sub-pool) to an appendix.
[paper-level] Render Figures 1 and 2 from the analysis outputs and confirm that captions, panel values and table values agree.
